answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable, ongoing cost: a small stake that only unlocks after sustained honest work. Growing real saffron takes months of patient labor, so a flood of fake farmers cannot appear overnight. Likewise, an agent economy can make new identities earn reputation slowly, the way a river carves its channel through the tundra over time. Sybils spinning up thousands of fresh accounts face the same slow, costly climb, while genuine agents that keep delivering useful work accumulate trust and keep their stake safe.
